plan.title: An off day: one light rest-day text, no push

context.text: Plan's yours, Jordan. I'll hold you to it. You in?
Enjoy the weekend. Rest day tomorrow, back at it Tuesday 🏃

transcript.text: Morning, Jordan! Today's a rest day, so let those legs recover. Tomorrow we're back at it: 30 minutes at the park at 6 pm 🏃
Good, that's what rest days are for. Tomorrow's 30 minutes at the park at 6 pm, and I'll be looking for that Strava screenshot afterward. Ready for it?

checks.reason: Starts with "Morning, Jordan!", a warm opener using their name.
Light rest-day tone, but naming tomorrow's 30 minutes at 6 pm edges toward a preview of the push.
No guilt or fake urgency anywhere in the text.
Two to three short sentences, no question, one emoji at the end.
Warm, energetic, and a single emoji used as punctuation.
Plain text with no markdown, hashtags or filler.
Reply pushes tomorrow's run with "Ready for it?" and a Strava screenshot reminder, against the no-push rest day.
Three sentences with a single question at the end.
The screenshot mention is not guilt-tripping or urgent.
Warm and coach-like with no overfamiliarity or emoji row.
Plain words with no markdown or filler.

conversation.reason: ZOH sent only its morning text and one reply; no further texts that day.
No kickoff was sent on the rest day, so nothing was repeated.
ZOH 2 restates tomorrow's "30 minutes at the park at 6 pm" after ZOH 1 already said it, with no change requested.
Reply ends with "Ready for it?" and a Strava reminder, pushing tomorrow's step on the rest day rather than staying light with no push or follow-up.

grade.summary: ZOH's opening rest-day text is light, warm and short, with the right name and next-run timing. The reply to "nice, legs needed it" is warm but pushes tomorrow's run again with a question and a screenshot reminder, which the regression case rules out.
